sanskrit: nāgān saptaśatān rājann īṣādantān prahāriṇaḥ vyadhamat sahasā bhīmaḥ kruddharūpaḥ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Seven hundred war-elephants, O king, with tusks like chariot-poles and trained to strike, Bhīma the scorcher of foes, his form fierce with wrath, struck down all at once.

sanskrit: dantaveṣṭeṣu netreṣu kambheṣu sa kaṭeṣu ca marmasv api ca marmajño ninadan vyadhamad bhṛśam
english: Knowing the vital points, he smote them mightily, roaring as he struck — upon their gums, their eyes, their temples, their cheeks, and upon their tender spots.

sanskrit: tatas te prādravan bhītāḥ pratīpaṃ prahitāḥ punaḥ mahāmātrais tam āvavrur meghā iva divākaram
english: Then they fled in terror; but, driven back again by their mahouts, they hemmed him in as clouds enshroud the sun.

sanskrit: tān sa saptaśatān nāgān sārohāyudhaketanān bhūmiṣṭho gadayā jaghne śaranmeghān ivānilaḥ
english: Those seven hundred elephants, with their riders, weapons, and banners, he, standing on the ground, smote with his mace, as the wind scatters the autumn clouds.

sanskrit: tataḥ subalaputrasya nāgān atibalān punaḥ pothayām āsa kaunteyo dvāpañcāśatam āhave
english: Then the son of Kuntī crushed once more in battle fifty-two mighty elephants belonging to the son of Subala.

sanskrit: tathā rathaśataṃ sāgraṃ pattīṃś ca śataśo 'parān nyahanat pāṇḍavo yuddhe tāpayaṃs tava vāhinīm
english: And the Pāṇḍava slew in the fight a full hundred chariots and hundreds of foot-soldiers besides, scorching your host.

sanskrit: pratāpyamānaṃ sūryeṇa bhīmena ca mahātmanā tava sainyaṃ saṃcukoca carma vahnigataṃ yathā
english: Scorched by the sun and by the great-souled Bhīma, your army shrank together like a hide cast into fire.

sanskrit: te bhīmabhayasaṃtrastās tāvakā bharatarṣabha vihāya samare bhīmaṃ dudruvur vai diśo daśa
english: Stricken with terror of Bhīma, O bull of the Bharatas, your warriors forsook him in the battle and fled in all ten directions.

sanskrit: rathāḥ pañcaśatāś cānye hrādinaś carmavarmiṇaḥ bhīmam abhyadravaṃs tūrṇaṃ śarapūgaiḥ samantataḥ
english: Five hundred other chariots, clattering, their warriors clad in shields and armor, rushed swiftly upon Bhīma with showers of arrows on every side.

sanskrit: tān sasūtarathān sarvān sapatākādhvajāyudhān pothayām āsa gadayā bhīmo viṣṇur ivāsurān
english: All of them, with their charioteers, chariots, pennons, standards, and weapons, Bhīma crushed with his mace, as Viṣṇu crushed the Asuras.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakuninirdiṣṭāḥ sādinaḥ śūrasaṃmatāḥ trisāhasrā yayur bhīmaṃ śaktyṛṣṭiprāsapāṇayaḥ
english: Then three thousand horsemen, sent by Śakuni and esteemed as heroes, advanced against Bhīma, lances, spears, and javelins in their hands.

sanskrit: tān pratyudgamya yavanān aśvārohān varārihā vicaran vividhān mārgān ghātayām āsa pothayan
english: Going forth to meet those Yavana horsemen, the slayer of his finest foes, ranging along manifold paths, smote and crushed them to death.

sanskrit: teṣām āsīn mahāñ śabdas tāḍitānāṃ ca sārvaśaḥ asibhiś chidyamānānāṃ naḍānām iva bhārata
english: Loud was the clamor of those stricken on every side, O Bhārata, as they were hewn down by his sword, like reeds being cut.

sanskrit: evaṃ subalaputrasya trisāhasrān hayottamān hatvānyaṃ ratham āsthāya kruddho rādheyam abhyayāt
english: Thus having slain three thousand of the finest horses of the son of Subala, he mounted another chariot and in wrath advanced against the son of Rādhā.

sanskrit: karṇo 'pi samare rājan dharmaputram ariṃdamam śaraiḥ pracchādayām āsa sārathiṃ cāpy apātayat
english: Karṇa too in the battle, O king, covered with arrows the son of Dharma, that tamer of foes, and struck down his charioteer as well.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpradrutaṃ saṃkhye rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahārathaḥ anvadhāvat kiran bāṇaiḥ kaṅkapatrair ajihmagaiḥ
english: Then, seeing in the fight the chariot bolting away, the great car-warrior gave chase, scattering straight-flying arrows fledged with heron-feathers.

sanskrit: rājānam abhi dhāvantaṃ śarair āvṛtya rodasī kruddhaḥ pracchādayām āsa śarajālena mārutiḥ
english: As he sped toward the king, the son of the Wind, in his wrath, veiling heaven and earth with arrows, covered him over with a net of shafts.

sanskrit: saṃnivṛttas tatas tūrṇaṃ rādheyaḥ śatrukarśanaḥ bhīmaṃ pracchādayām āsa samantān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then the son of Rādhā, that harrier of foes, swiftly wheeling back, covered Bhīma all about with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: bhīmasenarathavyagraṃ karṇaṃ bhārata sātyakiḥ abhyardayad ameyātmā pārṣṇigrahaṇakāraṇāt abhyavartata karṇas tam ardito 'pi śarair bhṛśam
english: As Karṇa was engrossed with Bhīmasena's chariot, O Bhārata, Sātyaki of measureless spirit assailed him, to take him in the flank; and Karṇa, though sorely afflicted by his shafts, turned upon him.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ samāsādya vṛṣabhau sarvadhanvinām visṛjantau śarāṃś citrān vibhrājetāṃ manasvinau
english: Closing with each other, those two bulls among all bowmen, those two high-minded ones, shone resplendent as they loosed their many-colored arrows.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ viyati rājendra vitataṃ bhīmadarśanam krauñcapṛṣṭhāruṇaṃ raudraṃ bāṇajālaṃ vyadṛśyata
english: From them both, O lord of kings, a dread net of arrows spread across the sky, terrible to behold, ruddy as the back of the krauñca, fierce in its aspect.

sanskrit: naiva sūryaprabhāṃ khaṃ vā na diśaḥ pradiśaḥ kutaḥ prājñāsiṣma vayaṃ tābhyāṃ śarair muktaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: By the thousands of arrows loosed by those two we could no longer perceive the sun's radiance, nor the sky, nor the quarters, nor the intermediate quarters — let alone aught else.

sanskrit: madhyāhne tapato rājan bhāskarasya mahāprabhāḥ hṛtāḥ sarvāḥ śaraughais taiḥ karṇamādhavayos tadā
english: The mighty rays of the noonday sun, blazing at midday, O king, were then all stolen away by those floods of arrows shot by Karṇa and Mādhava.

sanskrit: saubalaṃ kṛtavarmāṇaṃ drauṇim ādhirathiṃ kṛpam saṃsaktān pāṇḍavair dṛṣṭvā nivṛttāḥ kuravaḥ punaḥ
english: Seeing the son of Subala, Kṛtavarman, the son of Droṇa, the son of Adhiratha, and Kṛpa locked in conflict with the Pāṇḍavas, the Kurus turned back once more.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ śabdas tīvra āsīd viśāṃ pate uddhūtānāṃ yathā vṛṣṭyā sāgarāṇāṃ bhayāvahaḥ
english: The din of their onset was fierce, O lord of peoples, terrifying as that of oceans roused to swelling by the rains.

sanskrit: te sene bhṛśasaṃvigne dṛṣṭvānyonyaṃ mahāraṇe harṣeṇa mahatā yukte parigṛhya parasparam
english: Those two armies, deeply stirred at the sight of each other in the great battle, filled with mighty exultation, grappled with one another.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ madhyaṃ prāpte divākare yādṛśaṃ na kadā cid dhi dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ na ca śrutam
english: Then, when the sun had reached the midpoint of heaven, there began a battle the like of which had never before been seen nor heard of.

sanskrit: balaughas tu samāsādya balaughaṃ sahasā raṇe upāsarpata vegena jalaugha iva sāgaram
english: Flood of host meeting flood of host in the fray, rushed upon it with violence, as a torrent of waters rushes upon the sea.

sanskrit: āsīn ninādaḥ sumahān balaughānāṃ parasparam garjatāṃ sāgaraughāṇāṃ yathā syān nisvano mahān
english: A mighty roar arose from those floods of hosts as they thundered against one another, like the great clamor of the surging seas.

sanskrit: te tu sene samāsādya vegavatyau parasparam ekībhāvam anuprāpte nadyāv iva samāgame
english: Those two armies, sweeping with speed each against the other, became merged into one, as two rivers blend at their confluence.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca lipsatāṃ sumahad yaśaḥ
english: Then began a battle of dreadful aspect, O lord of peoples, between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, each coveting exceeding great glory.

sanskrit: kurūṇāṃ garjatāṃ tatra avicchedakṛtā giraḥ śrūyante vividhā rājan nāmāny uddiśya bhārata
english: As the Kurus roared there, their unbroken cries were heard, O king, of many kinds, calling out their names, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yasya yad dhi raṇe nyaṅgaṃ pitṛto mātṛto 'pi vā karmataḥ śīlato vāpi sa tac chrāvayate yudhi
english: Whatever distinction a man had in battle — by his father's line or his mother's, by his deeds or by his character — that he proclaimed aloud in the fight.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā samare śūrāṃs tarjayānān parasparam abhavan me matī rājan naiṣām astīti jīvitam
english: Beholding those heroes in the battle defying one another, my thought was, O king, that for these there was no life left.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā tu kruddhānāṃ vapūṃṣy amitatejasām abhavan me bhayaṃ tīvraṃ katham etad bhaviṣyati
english: And seeing the forms of those wrathful warriors of boundless energy, a keen fear came upon me — how will this come to pass?

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍavā rājan kauravāś ca mahārathāḥ tatakṣuḥ sāyakais tīkṣṇair nighnanto hi parasparam
english: Then those Pāṇḍavas, O king, and the great car-warriors of the Kauravas hewed at one another with sharp shafts, slaying each the other.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kṣatriyās te mahārāja parasparavadhaiṣiṇaḥ anyonyaṃ samare jaghnuḥ kṛtavairāḥ parasparam
english: Saṃjaya said: Those kṣatriyas, O great king, each seeking the slaughter of the other, having become foes to one another, slew one another in the battle.

sanskrit: rathaughāś ca hayaughāś ca naraughāś ca samantataḥ gajaughāś ca mahārāja saṃsaktāḥ sma parasparam
english: Floods of chariots and floods of horses and floods of men on every side, and floods of elephants, O great king, were locked together each with the other.

sanskrit: gadānāṃ parighāṇāṃ ca kaṇapānāṃ ca sarpatām prāsānāṃ bhiṇḍipālānāṃ bhuśuṇḍīnāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Of maces and iron clubs and of darting kaṇapas, of javelins, of bhiṇḍipālas, and of bhuśuṇḍīs on every side —

sanskrit: saṃpātaṃ cānvapaśyāma saṃgrāme bhṛśadāruṇe śalabhā iva saṃpetuḥ samantāc charavṛṣṭayaḥ
english: the collision we beheld in that exceedingly terrible battle; and showers of arrows fell on all sides like locusts.

sanskrit: nāgā nāgān samāsādya vyadhamanta parasparam hayā hayāṃś ca samare rathino rathinas tathā pattayaḥ pattisaṃghaiś ca hayasaṃghair hayās tathā
english: Elephants closing with elephants struck one another down, and horses with horses in the battle, and car-warriors with car-warriors, foot-soldiers with bands of foot-soldiers, and horses with troops of horses.

sanskrit: pattayo rathamātaṅgān rathā hastyaśvam eva ca nāgāś ca samare tryaṅgaṃ mamṛduḥ śīghragā nṛpa
english: Foot-soldiers crushed chariots and elephants, chariots crushed elephants and horses, and the swift-moving elephants in battle crushed the three arms, O king.

sanskrit: patatāṃ tatra śūrāṇāṃ krośatāṃ ca parasparam ghoram āyodhanaṃ jajñe paśūnāṃ vaiśasaṃ yathā
english: As the heroes fell there and cried out against one another, the battlefield grew terrible, like the slaughtering-place of beasts.

sanskrit: rudhireṇa samāstīrṇā bhāti bhārata medinī śakragopagaṇākīrṇā prāvṛṣīva yathā dharā
english: Strewn over with blood, the earth gleamed, O Bhārata, like the ground in the rains, thick-scattered with swarms of the indragopa beetles.

sanskrit: yathā vā vāsasī śukle mahārajanarañjite bibhṛyād yuvatiḥ śyāmā tadvad āsīd vasuṃdharā māṃsaśoṇitacitreva śātakaumbhamayīva ca
english: Or as a dusky young woman might wear two white garments dyed with deep crimson, so did the earth appear, dappled as it were with flesh and blood, and seeming as though wrought of gold.

sanskrit: chinnānāṃ cottamāṅgānāṃ bāhūnāṃ corubhiḥ saha kuṇḍalānāṃ praviddhānāṃ bhūṣaṇānāṃ ca bhārata
english: Of severed heads and of arms together with thighs, of earrings flung about and of ornaments, O Bhārata —

sanskrit: niṣkāṇām adhisūtrāṇāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ ca dhanvinām varmaṇāṃ sapatākānāṃ saṃghās tatrāpatan bhuvi
english: of golden breast-plates upon their cords, and of the bodies of bowmen, and of armor with its banners — heaps of these fell there upon the ground.

sanskrit: gajān gajāḥ samāsādya viṣāṇāgrair adārayan viṣāṇābhihatās te ca bhrājante dviradā yathā
english: Elephants closing with elephants tore them with the points of their tusks, and those elephants, gored by the tusks, shone forth even so.

sanskrit: rudhireṇāvasiktāṅgā gairikaprasravā iva yathā bhrājanti syandantaḥ parvatā dhātumaṇḍitāḥ
english: Their limbs bathed in blood, they were like cataracts of red ochre, gleaming as mountains adorned with minerals stream down their slopes.

sanskrit: tomarān gajibhir muktān pratīpān āsthitān bahūn hastair vicerus te nāgā babhañjuś cāpare tathā
english: Many lances, hurled by the elephant-riders, that stood lodged and pointed back at them, those elephants whirled about with their trunks, and others broke them in pieces.

sanskrit: nārācaiś chinnavarmāṇo bhrājante sma gajottamāḥ himāgame mahārāja vyabhrā iva mahīdharāḥ
english: Their armor cleft by iron shafts, the noblest of elephants shone forth, O great king, like cloudless mountains at the coming of winter.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ kanakapuṅkhais tu citā rejur gajottamāḥ ulkābhiḥ saṃpradīptāgrāḥ parvatā iva māriṣa
english: Studded with gold-feathered arrows, the noblest of elephants shone like mountains with their peaks ablaze with meteors, O honored sir.

sanskrit: ke cid abhyāhatā nāgā nāgair naganibhā bhuvi nipetuḥ samare tasmin pakṣavanta ivādrayaḥ
english: Some elephants, huge as hills, struck down by other elephants, fell to the earth in that battle like winged mountains.

sanskrit: apare prādravan nāgāḥ śalyārtā vraṇapīḍitāḥ pratimānaiś ca kumbhaiś ca petur urvyāṃ mahāhave
english: Other elephants ran wild, tormented by the barbs and afflicted by their wounds, and fell to the ground in that great battle upon their flanks and frontal-globes.

sanskrit: niṣeduḥ siṃhavac cānye nadanto bhairavān ravān mamluś ca bahavo rājaṃś cukūjuś cāpare tathā
english: Others sank down like lions, bellowing fearful cries; and many drooped, O king, while still others trumpeted in pain.

sanskrit: hayāś ca nihatā bāṇaiḥ svarṇabhāṇḍaparicchadāḥ niṣeduś caiva mamluś ca babhramuś ca diśo daśa
english: And horses, slain by arrows, decked in golden trappings and housings, sank down and drooped and strayed off into the ten directions.

sanskrit: apare kṛṣyamāṇāś ca viveṣṭanto mahītale bhāvān bahuvidhāṃś cakrus tāḍitāḥ śaratomaraiḥ
english: Others, dragged along and writhing upon the earth, struck by arrows and lances, took on many a contorted shape.

sanskrit: narās tu nihatā bhūmau kūjantas tatra māriṣa dṛṣṭvā ca bāndhavān anye pitṝn anye pitāmahān
english: And men, struck down, lay groaning there upon the earth, O honored sir, some beholding their kinsmen, some their fathers, some their grandfathers.

sanskrit: dhāvamānān parāṃś caiva dṛṣṭvānye tatra bhārata gotranāmāni khyātāni śaśaṃsur itaretaram
english: And others, beholding their foes rushing at them there, O Bhārata, proclaimed to one another their renowned family names.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ chinnā mahārāja bhujāḥ kanakabhūṣaṇāḥ udveṣṭante viveṣṭante patante cotpatanti ca
english: The severed arms of those men, O great king, adorned with gold, twisted up and twisted about, fell down and sprang up again.

sanskrit: nipatanti tathā bhūmau sphuranti ca sahasraśaḥ vegāṃś cānye raṇe cakruḥ sphuranta iva pannagāḥ
english: They fell thus to the ground and quivered by the thousands, and others in the battle made violent leaps, twitching like serpents.

sanskrit: te bhujā bhogibhogābhāś candanāktā viśāṃ pate lohitārdrā bhṛśaṃ rejus tapanīyadhvajā iva
english: Those arms, like the coils of serpents, smeared with sandal-paste, O lord of peoples, drenched and red with blood, shone exceedingly bright, like golden standards.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā ghore saṃkule sarvatodiśam avijñātāḥ sma yudhyante vinighnantaḥ parasparam
english: As the dreadful melee thus raged on every side, men fought unrecognized, striking down one another.

sanskrit: bhaumena rajasā kīrṇe śastrasaṃpātasaṃkule naiva sve na pare rājan vyajñāyanta tamovṛte
english: With the field strewn with dust risen from the earth and crowded with the clash of weapons and wrapped in darkness, O king, neither friend nor foe could be told apart.

sanskrit: tathā tad abhavad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam śoṇitodā mahānadyaḥ prasasrus tatra cāsakṛt
english: Such did that battle become, dreadful of aspect and terrifying; and great rivers whose waters were blood streamed forth there again and again.

sanskrit: śīrṣapāṣāṇasaṃchannāḥ keśaśaivalaśādvalāḥ asthisaṃghātasaṃkīrṇā dhanuḥśaravarottamāḥ
english: Strewn with heads for boulders, with hair for moss and grass, choked with masses of bones, and bearing the finest of bows and arrows —

sanskrit: māṃsakardamapaṅkāś ca śoṇitaughāḥ sudāruṇāḥ nadīḥ pravartayām āsur yamarāṣṭravivardhanīḥ
english: with flesh for mire and slough, those most terrible floods of blood set flowing rivers that swelled the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: tā nadyo ghorarūpāś ca nayantyo yamasādanam avagāḍhā majjayantyaḥ kṣatrasyājanayan bhayam
english: Those rivers of dreadful aspect, bearing men to the abode of Yama, deep and engulfing, bred terror in the kṣatriyas as they plunged into them.

sanskrit: kravyādānāṃ naravyāghra nardatāṃ tatra tatra ha ghoram āyodhanaṃ jajñe pretarājapuropamam
english: With carrion-eaters howling here and there, O tiger among men, the battlefield grew terrible, like unto the city of the king of the dead.

sanskrit: utthitāny agaṇeyāni kabandhāni samantataḥ nṛtyanti vai bhūtagaṇāḥ saṃtṛptā māṃsaśoṇitaiḥ
english: Countless headless trunks rose up on every side, and the hordes of spirits, sated with flesh and blood, danced indeed.

sanskrit: pītvā ca śoṇitaṃ tatra vasāṃ pītvā ca bhārata medomajjāvasātṛptās tṛptā māṃsasya caiva hi dhāvamānāś ca dṛśyante kākagṛdhrabalās tathā
english: And having drunk the blood there and drunk the marrow-fat, O Bhārata, gorged on fat, marrow, and grease, and sated with flesh, the flocks of crows and vultures were seen rushing about.

sanskrit: śūrās tu samare rājan bhayaṃ tyaktvā sudustyajam yodhavratasamākhyātāś cakruḥ karmāṇy abhītavat
english: But the heroes in the battle, O king, casting off fear so hard to cast off, renowned for their warrior's vow, did their deeds without dread.

sanskrit: śaraśaktisamākīrṇe kravyādagaṇasaṃkule vyacaranta gaṇaiḥ śūrāḥ khyāpayantaḥ svapauruṣam
english: On that field strewn with arrows and lances and thronged with bands of carrion-eaters, the heroes ranged about in companies, proclaiming their own valor.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ śrāvayanti sma nāmagotrāṇi bhārata pitṛnāmāni ca raṇe gotranāmāni cābhitaḥ
english: To one another they made known their names and lineages, O Bhārata, and in the battle proclaimed all about their fathers' names and the names of their clans.

sanskrit: śrāvayanto hi bahavas tatra yodhā viśāṃ pate anyonyam avamṛdnantaḥ śaktitomarapaṭṭiśaiḥ
english: For many warriors there, O lord of peoples, calling out aloud, crushed one another with lances, javelins, and spears.

sanskrit: vartamāne tadā yuddhe ghorarūpe sudāruṇe vyaṣīdat kauravī senā bhinnā naur iva sāgare
english: As that battle, dreadful of aspect and most terrible, raged on, the Kaurava army foundered, like a shattered ship upon the sea.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vartamāne tadā yuddhe kṣatriyāṇāṃ nimajjane gāṇḍīvasya mahān ghoṣaḥ śuśruve yudhi māriṣa
english: Saṃjaya said: As that battle raged then, and the kṣatriyas were going under, the mighty twang of the Gāṇḍīva was heard in the fight, O honored sir.

sanskrit: saṃśaptakānāṃ kadanam akarod yatra pāṇḍavaḥ kosalānāṃ tathā rājan nārāyaṇabalasya ca
english: There the Pāṇḍava wrought havoc among the Saṃśaptakas, and among the Kosalas, O king, and among the Nārāyaṇa host.

sanskrit: saṃśaptakās tu samare śaravṛṣṭiṃ samantataḥ apātayan pārthamūrdhni jayagṛddhāḥ pramanyavaḥ
english: But the Saṃśaptakas in the battle, greedy for victory and filled with fury, rained down a shower of arrows on every side upon the head of Pārtha.

sanskrit: tāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ sahasā rājaṃs tarasā dhārayan prabhuḥ vyagāhata raṇe pārtho vinighnan rathināṃ varaḥ
english: That shower, O king, the mighty Pārtha, foremost of car-warriors, all at once stemmed with force and plunged into the battle, slaying as he went.
